summary:
What if the Moon could tell us stories about the missions that changed our understanding of space?

LAST SIGNAL is a browser-based 3D lunar exploration game that invites learners aged 10–15 to uncover the forgotten stories of NASA's lunar equipment. Players step into an astronaut's role, explore a virtual lunar landscape, investigate abandoned equipment, and discover the science and history behind each object.

But exploration is only the beginning. Players face simulated mission decisions, see how their choices compare with real historical events, access learning resources, and test their understanding through interactive recall challenges.

Inspired by NASA's “Abandoned but Not Forgotten” challenge, LAST SIGNAL transforms the legacy of lunar equipment into an interactive journey of discovery. It aims to make space science more immersive by giving learners the opportunity to explore, question, decide, and remember — rather than simply observe.

Because even when a mission ends, its discoveries leave a signal worth following.
details:
LAST SIGNAL — Project Details

What does it do?

LAST SIGNAL is an interactive, browser-based 3D lunar exploration game designed for learners aged 10–15. It transforms the Moon into an explorable learning environment where players take on the role of an astronaut and uncover the stories behind NASA's lunar equipment.

Players can navigate a virtual lunar landscape, discover abandoned equipment, interact with objects, and access educational panels explaining their purpose, scientific importance, and connection to past missions. The experience also includes mission objectives, simulated decision-making scenarios, historical comparisons, educational resources, and interactive quizzes that encourage active recall.

How does it address the challenge?

Inspired by NASA's "Abandoned but Not Forgotten" challenge, LAST SIGNAL brings attention to the equipment left behind during lunar exploration. Rather than presenting these objects as forgotten hardware, it explores them as valuable parts of humanity's scientific history. Players discover what the equipment was designed to do and how it contributed to our understanding of the Moon.

Benefits and intended impact

The project aims to make space science more accessible, engaging, and interactive for young learners. It encourages curiosity, exploration, critical thinking, and learning through decision-making. By combining discovery with quizzes and historical comparisons, LAST SIGNAL creates opportunities for learners to engage with scientific information and actively recall what they have learned.

Its intended impact is to inspire greater interest in space exploration while helping students connect scientific discoveries with the missions and equipment that made them possible.

Tools and technologies

The project was developed as a web-based experience using:

  • React and TypeScript for the user interface and application logic.
  • Three.js for the interactive 3D lunar environment.
  • Vite as the development and build tool.
  • Tailwind CSS for interface styling.
  • GitHub for source-code version control.
  • Vercel for public deployment and web hosting.

Creativity and innovation

The central idea behind LAST SIGNAL is to turn historical space equipment into interactive discoveries. Its distinctive learning loop combines exploration, investigation, decision-making, and active recall. One key feature allows players to make a simulated mission decision and then compare their choice with what actually happened in history.

This connects gameplay with real-world scientific history, making the learning experience more than a virtual tour.

Factors considered

During development, we considered the target age group, ease of navigation, accessibility through a web browser, educational clarity, scientific accuracy, and the balance between gameplay and learning. We also aimed to keep the experience focused on lunar exploration, with clear distinctions between simulated scenarios and historical facts.

LAST SIGNAL is built around one idea: equipment may be left behind, but the discoveries and stories it carries should never be forgotten.
